capability: Evaluate a Cauchy transform with kernel-aware near-axis quadrature and caller-resolved density features.

excluded: Callback-only whole-line support discovery (fails closed because it is information-limited).
Source-project MATLAB behavior, graphics, global root scans and arbitrary analytic continuation.
preconditions: Density returns finite real numeric scalar samples; the Cauchy integral exists on the selected contour.

Caller bounds or mesh resolve all material density features; whole-line tails are integrable and contain no unresolved density features. The integrator resolves the known kernel peak without requiring the caller to mesh the pole-height scale.
supported: Finite ordered bounds already resolving the callback support.
Whole-line integration with an explicit finite increasing integration_mesh that resolves support/features and integrable tails.

example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.kinetic import evaluate_cauchy_transform
mesh=np.linspace(-10,10,81)
r=evaluate_cauchy_transform(0.4+0.7j,lambda v: np.exp(-v*v)/np.sqrt(np.pi),integration_mesh=mesh)
assert np.isfinite(r["G"])
example.description: Integrate a normalized Gaussian with an explicit finite feature mesh.
example.expected: Observed PASS: the explicit 81-point mesh gives a finite complex G and two component quadrature-error estimates.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for invalid, nonfinite, singular or incompatible inputs, including epsabs/epsrel=None or non-scalar values and callback-only whole-line integration without integration_mesh.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Raises RuntimeError if any QUADPACK panel reports nonconvergence; no partial result is returned.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial scientific result is returned after a failed call.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Callback exceptions propagate; invalid callback output or unrepresentable result raises ValueError.

assumptions: The callback is finite on every integrated panel.
For bounds=null, integration_mesh explicitly partitions material support/features and the two tails are integrable.
A generic callback cannot certify unseen density support from adaptive samples; the known Cauchy kernel scale is handled internally. Error estimates remain conditional.
identity.coordinates: Complex phase point and real integration coordinate
identity.definition: For z=x+i*y, near-projection finite panels use v=x+abs(y)*sinh(t), giving density(v)*(tanh(t)+i*sign(y)*sech(t)) dt. Bounded transformed panels resolve the known kernel peak and long tails; smooth far panels and infinite tails use real-coordinate quadrature. Explicit analytic continuation is added only under the stated support policy.

inputs.description: Complex phase points off the real axis.
inputs.name: z

inputs.constraints: Callable returning finite real numeric scalars at all sampled velocities; caller declares feature resolution.
inputs.description: Real density callback of one real velocity.
inputs.name: density

inputs.constraints: None selects whole-line mode with required mesh; otherwise finite ordered real pair; booleans and complex coordinates rejected.
inputs.name: bounds

inputs.constraints: None or callable returning finite numeric scalars, representing the analytic extension of the same density. Finite-bound continuation only for strict a < Re(z) < b.
inputs.description: Optional analytic extension for lower-plane continuation.
inputs.name: analytic_density

inputs.constraints: Strictly increasing finite points; with bounds, mesh must lie inside bounds. When bounds is null, mesh endpoints delimit a resolved feature region and infinite tails are also integrated.
inputs.description: Finite strictly increasing real mesh partitioning material support/features; required when bounds is null.
inputs.name: integration_mesh
inputs.shape: one-dimensional array with at least two points

outputs.description: Summed real/imaginary quadrature indicators with floating accumulation allowances, including continuation; not bounds on callback or analytic-extension errors.
outputs.name: quadrature_error

python.signature: evaluate_cauchy_transform(z, density, *, bounds=None, analytic_density=None, epsabs=1e-10, epsrel=1e-10, limit=200, integration_mesh=None)

summary: Evaluate a Cauchy transform with kernel-aware near-axis quadrature and caller-resolved density features.

scope: Independent basis: in the upper half plane the transform of a normalized Gaussian equals the plasma dispersion function Z(z) = i sqrt(pi) exp(-z**2) erfc(-i z), recomputed at 40 digits from erfc; measured agreement is at the 1e-11 level on a 561-point mesh, so the floor belongs to the transform's own quadrature.

A uniform density on [-1, 1] is checked against its closed form, 0.5 log((z-1)/(z+1)); the sign was measured rather than assumed, because the opposite ordering differs by exactly -1, which appears as a relative error of 2.0 rather than as a small residual.

The branch below the real axis is established as a relation: the port returns conj(G(conj(z))) rather than Z(z), and the two differ by about 2.9 in the real part, so this is a branch statement and not an identity that any correct implementation would satisfy.

Failure matrix: one assertion per channel -- the transform kernel, the lower-half-plane branch, the sign of the closed form, and a conjugate or imaginary-part error, which a modulus comparison would not see.

Precision budget, written before measurement: 1e-10 on the Gaussian closed form, 1e-12 on the conjugate-symmetry relation, 1e-10 on the uniform closed form, and a separation of more than 1.0 between the returned lower-half-plane value and the direct analytic continuation.
The mesh densities are stated so the quadrature floor is attributable: the Gaussian is integrated on a 561-point mesh over [-14, 14] and the uniform density on 401 points over its support.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Bounded to two densities with closed forms (normalized Gaussian, uniform on a finite support) and to complex phases on both sides of the real axis, with the branch choice pinned by a conjugate-symmetry relation. Established by the plasma dispersion function recomputed at 40 digits from erfc, by a closed-form integral, and by a branch relation whose two sides differ by more than 1.0. Excluded scope: densities with unresolved features, the 2 pi i residue term that a different continuation would carry, and any statement about the transform exactly on the real axis.
known_limitations: The returned value below the real axis is the conjugate-reflected branch, not the direct analytic continuation Z(z); the contract states the branch the port implements and does not claim the other one.
Densities whose features the quadrature cannot resolve are outside this evidence; the port's own resolution contract governs them.

The `swap` mutation is covered, not killed, and its surface has no owner: the only multi-element array the port returns is `quadrature_error`, and no contract in this repository declares any property of it. That is a capability boundary of the whole catalog, not merely something this contract does not look at.

basis.statement: A branch relation is checked whose two sides differ by more than 1.0. Excluded scope: densities with unresolved features, the 2*pi*i residue term that a different continuation would carry, and any statement about the transform exactly on the real axis.

references: Hua-Sheng Xie, Generalized plasma dispersion function, Phys. Plasmas. 20 (2013), 092125 (scientific context)
